body:
# C3 — Health hooks: failure-triggered checks that troubleshoot and report

Component of the reporting-architecture program (starter epic #9568).
Source: Drew's directive, Reports chat, 2026-11-13 09:11 CST.
Statements: S1.3.

## Scope

Checks like **"PM stack reachable"** and **"OpenCode working"** stop being
interval polls and become **hook scripts that fire on failure-to-connect**:

- On a failed connect (from any caller: PM stack surfaces, lane launches,
  aggregator ticks), the hook fires immediately, runs a bounded
  troubleshoot sequence (reachability, service state, auth/credential
  health, recent changes), and **reports what occurred** — a note to the
  queues/PM-health category chat, escalating to Reports when it is an
  exception and to the main chat when Drew is blocked.
- The hook records the incident into the PM-stack event store so C6 can
  render an incident page and C8 can ingest it (first-appearance data for
  error strings starts here).
- Recovery is also an event: the same hook reports the recovery (the
  watchdog's new-alert/recovery pattern, event-driven).

## Boundaries / collisions

- This is the successor to the **disabled** opencode-session-minder's
  detection role — hooks, not a revived cron (the Fleet CA coordinator's
  finding stands: no durable monitor covered sessions after 2026-11-08;
  this component closes that gap by trigger, not by schedule).
- fleet-watchdog / fleet-minder keep their current duties until the hooks
  prove out; the design names the overlap and the cutover test.
- Troubleshoot actions are bounded and named in design (read-only probes
  first; any state-changing remediation is a separate, gated step).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Merged design: trigger surface (who calls, what counts as
      failure-to-connect), probe sequence per check, report format,
      escalation rules.
- [ ] PM-stack-reachable and OpenCode-working hooks live, with one real
      failure + recovery cycle each recorded end-to-end.
- [ ] Incident records land in the event store in the shape C6/C8 consume.
